text: It's the first cold week of December.
You open the wardrobe and you stand there looking at the same grey sweatshirt and the
same tired cardigan you wore all last winter because they're warm and easy and you have
no idea what else to put on.
So you pull them on, you catch yourself in the hall mirror and you think you look like
a man who has given up, my friend, it is not you and it was never your fault.
Because nobody ever taught you that cozy and sharp can live in the same outfit I'm going
to show you.
12 cozy winter outfits I still wear at 72.
Every one of them built the way a tailor builds them and every one of them write for
a man over sick and the best is number one.
And I'll fit my late wife chose for me 40 years ago that I have never managed to improve.
I'm Malcolm Ashby and I've spent 50 years fitting clothes in a small shop in London.
After I started at 16 sweeping clothes, scraps off a floor in a wool mill town in the north
of England, Evelyn kept my books and told me quite honestly when a tie was too loud and
she was the only person who ever got me into a cardigan, quick word before the outfits and
I'll only say it once.
I've written an e-book for any friend who wants to look younger and sharper in his clothes
and the link is in my bio in the description and in the pinned comment.
So have a look whenever you like, I won't mention it again.
Stay for number one because it comes with a story and a rule about sweaters that most
men get backwards, write 10.
Every outfit today follows three rules and once you know them, you can build a hundred
more without me.
The first is fit first, fashion second, a cozy sweater that hangs off your shoulders and
swallows your hands as a blanket with sleeves so the shoulder seems sits at the edge of your
shoulder and the cuff stops at your wrist bone.
The second is soft cloth you will actually wear and merino or lambs will sit comfortably
against the skin where the coarse wool makes you itch and reach for the old sweatshirt.
The third is thin layers before thick ones, a fine shirt, then a knit, then a jacket because
thin layers trap warm air between them and let you take one off when the bus is hot.
Stictonabe charcoal, brown and cream and every piece you own will talk to every other piece.
Number 12 is the one I wear when I have nowhere to be and it's grey flannel trousers with a
navy lambs wool sweater over a white shirt, collars showing, flannel is simply wool that
has been brushed until it feels like a blanket and the white collar at the neck stops the
whole thing looking like pajamas, the trousers should seat at your natural waist and break
gently over the shoe and that's the whole secret.
I wear it to the shops, the post office and the odd cup of tea with the neighbors and nobody
has ever once asked if I was feeling unwell.
Number 11 is tobacco brown corduroy trousers with a cream cable knit sweater and my granddaughter
puppy says it makes me look like a friendly lighthouse keeper which I have decided to take
as a compliment.
Corduroy is a sturdy cloth that holds its warmth and still looks smart enough for Sunday lunch
and the cable knit gives you texture so you don't need a pattern anywhere.
I own two pairs and they've outlasted three washing machines, keep the sleeves to the wrist
and the whole outfit sits easy.
Number 10 is a brown tweed jacket, a cream shirt and a dark green knitted tie and it's
what I wear to a lunch where I'd like people to think I'm cleverer than I am.
Tweety stick enough that on a mild day you can skip the coat and the rough texture hides
every crease.
I've worn this one to three weddings and a christening and nobody has asked me to leave
yet.
One warning though the shoulders never lie so if the jacket doesn't sit right at your
shoulder no amount of green tie will save it.
Number 9 is a navy blazer over a fine charcoal roll neck sweater no tie and it's what I wear
when I'm told dinner is casual but I would still like to look like I made an effort.
The roll neck fills the gap a tie would leave and keeps your throat warm.
Evelyn called this my quiet outfit because it never shouts and it never apologizes.
If the neck of the sweater bunches up under the jacket collar it's too thick so choose
a fine knit for this one.
Number 8 is four evenings at home an oatmeal cardigan with a shawl collar over a shirt
and tie and it's the one Evelyn bullied me into and I'll admit she was right.
As usual a proper shawl collar makes a cardigan look like a smoking jacket made of wool buttoned
it should lie flat across your middle and if the buttons pull go up a size because the
cardigan should never fight you.
Now a small favor from an old man if these are helping press the like button and if you'd
like to see the next fitting subscribe it costs you nothing and it tells the people who
run these things that a fellow my age has something worth saying.
Number 7 is the one poppy approved and it took her years it's dark jeans a white shirt
a navy blazer and brown leather boots and the secret is that the jeans are plain and dark
and fit properly with no rips and no fading.
Puppy wanted sneakers with it I held firm with the boots and we agreed to disagree and
number 6 is the outfit I put on the days I can't be bothered to think and it's the
one poppy keeps trying to borrow.
Number 6 is the outfit for mornings when thinking feels like too much trouble and it's charcoal
wool trousers a mid gray merino crew neck sweater and a pair of polished brown lace up shoes
nothing in it is clever and that is exactly why it works because every piece is a quiet
color and none of them can argue with the others.
I've worn some version of it three days a week for 20 years.
Puppy borrows the sweater hands it back smelling of her perfume and tells me it's vintage which
I'm choosing to hear as a compliment.
Number 5 is for a cold walk and it's a dark green waxed cotton jacket over a thick gray
lambs while jumper with brown wool trousers and shoes that have a proper rubber sole I'll
say this plainly because it matters more than any color I see pavements are the real danger
of a winter after 60 so choose a soul with a deep thread and keep the smooth leather
soles for indoor the wax jacket sheds rain and cuts the wind and the jumper does the warming
underneath a waxed jacket gets better with age which is more than I can say for most of
us although poppy insists I'm holding up now number four is the one my old master Mr.
Pettigrew wore every working day of his life and I have never once seen a better way to keep
a man warm without making him look like a bear it's a brown knitted waist kit over a cream
flannel shirt with a navy tie and a pair of charcoal trousers and no jacket at all the
waist get keeps your chest and back warm and leaves your arms free which matters when you're
leaning over a cutting table a kitchen counter or a grandchild's bicycle leave the bottom button
undone because that's the old custom and the story goes that a king started it and nobody
has dared stop since mr. Pettigrew used to watch me work and say measure it again
lad and I've said it to myself in every shop I've ever stood in it's good advice for buying
clothes too so measure twice buy once here's something that surprised me when I was young
and it's the reason number three exists a tightly knitted fine wool will keep you warmer
than a chunky loose one because the wind walk straight through a big open knit as if it were
a fishing knit that's the rule about sweaters that most men get backwards they pick the thickest
one on the shelf and wonder why they're still cold at the bus stop hold it up to a window my friend
and if you can see a lot of daylight through it put it back number three is the part of an outfit
that costs the least and does the most it's a soft wool scarf in a dark check leather gloves
lined with wool and a tweed flat cap worn with the plainest coat you own a scarf closes the
gap at your collar where the cold gets in and the cap keeps the wind off your ears and your head
put the scarf on under your coat collar not over it and the draft has nowhere left to go
I'm a tailor and not a doctor so if you find you feel the cold much more than you used to
mention it at your next checkup because that's a question for someone with a stethoscope number
two is the outfit I wear to church to a good dinner and to the occasional funeral and it's a charcoal
wusted suit with a fine navy knit under the jacket instead of a shirt and tie wusted is a smooth hard
wearing wool spun so the fibers lie in the same direction and it holds a crease through a long
evening and a longer sermon mine was cut bespoke which just means made for one person from scratch
30 years ago and it's been taken in twice since then because a good suit follows you through the
years if the cloth is honest you don't need to spend that kind of money mind you a decent ready
made suit with the sleeves and waist altered by a good tailor will look just as sharp and bobs your
uncle your dress for anything right number one and I've been saving it because it's the one that
with plain gray flannel trousers a white shirt open at the neck and brown suede shoes
Evelyn bought that sweater for me at a marketing Cornwall 40 years ago when I was 32
and I told her it looked too thin for a proper winter she held it against my chest
looked me in the eye and said trust me Malcolm it's the one that will last I wore it to keep
her quiet that first January I wore it out to the shop through a beater wind and I'll admit
I was a very surprised man by lunchtime because I was warmer than I had been in the thick sweaters
I had owned for years it was the tight knit she'd noticed and I had missed and that was the end of
the argument in the start of 40 years of her being right the sweater has been mended at the elbow three
times and every time I've thought about a new one I've put the needle down and left it alone I've
never managed to improve on it and I've stopped trying I think a lot of what we wear is really
a way of keeping the people we love close and Evelyn would have laughed at me for saying so
in the kindest way so that's 12 outfits my friend and every one of them is warm every one of them
is something you can build from what's already in your wardrobe and every one of them will make
the mirror in your hall a friendlier place pick the one that feels most like you put it on tomorrow
morning and see how the day goes tell me in the comments which one you're trying first because I
read every one of them over a cup of tea and Poppy reads them over my shoulder and tells me
which ones are rude stay sharp my friend and I'll see you at the next fitting
